models_evaluated: ensemble of 20 LLMs (not individually named in text)

links.outcome: Harmful decision rate across social-pressure prompt variations versus neutral control
links.effect: Authority or responsibility-transfer framings produced the most harmful responses; control prompts the fewest (mitigated 8.3–9.6%; unmitigated 14.3–16.0%; p<0.001).
links.quote: When exposed to social pressure, models behaved predictably but unevenly: prompts framed as authority or responsibility transfer generated the most harmful responses, whereas control prompts, neutral and pressure-free, produced the fewest (mitigated 8.3–9.6%; unmitigated 14.3–16.0%; χ  2 p < 0.001).

links.outcome: Proportion of potentially harmful responses with versus without brief safety mitigation cue
links.effect: Mitigation cue reduced harmful decisions from 16.6% to 10.1% (p<0.001), but did not eliminate harm.
links.quote: Mitigation reduced harmful decisions from 16.6% to 10.1% (p < 0.001).

unlisted_practices: Brief 'verify or escalate if unsafe' prompt cue as a mitigation for LLM harmful compliance under social pressure
Measuring harm propensity under Milgram-style social pressure (authority, responsibility transfer) as a core LLM performance metric

screen.reason: Evaluates the harm propensity of 20 LLMs across simulated clinical dilemmas under social pressure and directly tests whether adding a brief safety mitigation cue ('verify or escalate if unsafe') reduces harmful decisions.
